I farm only 1.5 mu, so I count every bag of input. I do not make a fancy plan from zero. I start from what worked for me before in this wheat-maize rotation, then I adjust a little. In Quzhou our land can still give a decent crop if water keeps up and I do not let fertilizer run short. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield, because with such a small area a bad harvest hurts more than a little extra cost. For wheat, I will keep improved seed, put the base fertilizer down before or at sowing, then topdress nitrogen when the seedlings recover and again around jointing if the stand looks strong. Since I have well irrigation, I will use it at the key times instead of gambling on rain. For maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed like most people around here, because the hybrids give steadier ears and better yield if water and fertilizer keep up. I will give maize a heavier nitrogen dose than wheat, keep phosphorus and potassium in the ground, water at the important stages, and spray when I see real pressure from weeds, armyworm, aphids, rust, or leaf disease. On 1.5 mu I will still do most work with family, so I will keep the system simple: rotary tillage after each harvest, improved or hybrid seed, enough fertilizer, and not too many unnecessary pesticide passes.
